shorts.title: What you will learn: std::map
shorts.hook: Look up a value by its name.
shorts.script: Look up a value by its name. Today we look things up by name. A map stores keys and values, and keeps the keys in sorted order. A map stores pairs. Each pair has a key and a value. Keys are unique, and the map keeps them sorted. You use the key to find the value. Square brackets read a value. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: std::map.

shorts.title: std::map in one minute
shorts.script: A map stores pairs. Each pair has a key and a value. Keys are unique, and the map keeps them sorted. You use the key to find the value. Square brackets read a value. But beware. If the key is missing, square brackets create it. Think of a phone book. You look up a name, and you get a number. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: std::map in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.hook: We start the map with a list of pairs.
shorts.script: We start the map with a list of pairs. The loop unpacks each pair into a name and marks. The order is sorted by key. Asha, Meera, then Ravi. Find looks up a key without creating it. If it equals end, the key is missing. Otherwise, second is the value. The program prints Asha, Meera and Ravi with their marks, and then Found eighty-eight. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: A lookup that creates a key
shorts.hook: Can you spot the bug in std map?
shorts.script: Can you spot the bug in std map? Bug of the Day. We only wanted to check for Ravi. But the size is two, not one. Square brackets created the key Ravi, with the value zero. Use count or find to check without changing the map. Square brackets create a missing key with a default value. So a simple look-up grows the map. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: A lookup that creates a key.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: Can you count the marks in std map?
shorts.script: Can you count the marks in std map? My map was lost. It had all the keys, but no values. Make a map from names to marks. Add three students. Print the one with the highest marks. Write your answer in the comments. A map stores key and value pairs. Keys are unique and sorted. Square brackets read or create a key. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Pun and challenge.
